note: Independent semantic rejudgment 2026-11-12 against the complete Section 2.3 Attributes paragraph, including mandatory attributes, changes that cannot be carried out, and unsupported attribute types/values for BOTH CoA and Disconnect. Existing UnsupportedAttributeNAKed and CoAWithAnUnsupportedAttributeValueIsNAKed require exact NAKs for unsupported types and sole invalid values; CoAWithOneUnsupportedValueBesideSupportedOnesIsNAKed keeps a supported rate beside an invalid second Filter-Id/duplicate rate/unknown vendor, requiring 407 and no emitted change. DisconnectWithAnUnsupportedValueIsNAKed isolates malformed NAS-Port versus unsupported VSA, requires 407/401 and zero teardown. RequestWhoseEveryValueIsSupportedIsACKed retains useful CoA and Disconnect acceptance. New DynamicAuthorizationRefusesUnimplementedIdentification supplies valid signed wire encodings of each of eleven unsupported identification types, one at a time alongside all three matching supported selectors, for both request kinds: NAK 401, both shaping directions unchanged, subscriber retained and no teardown. CoAImplementedIdentificationStillApplies uses only the three implemented selectors and explicit 20mbit/5mbit, requiring signed ACK and those actual backend rates. Section 2.3 expressly allows a NAS to omit CoA support for attributes it supports in authentication/accounting, so explicit 401 replaces the former silent ignore correctly. readCoAChange walks every authorization attribute; unsupportedAttr/unsupportedAttrValue run before application; the companion atomicity units enforce unavailable-backend refusal rather than event-only success. Accepting/ignoring any of these extras or values breaks the exact NAK/no-change controls; blanket refusal breaks useful ACK controls. Native proof freshness remains main's separate gate.
